name: Renters insurance (California)
definition: The policy a tenant buys for the half of the building the landlord does not insure. The regulator states it plainly: the landlord does not provide insurance for the tenant's personal property [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]. A renters policy carries personal property, loss of use, personal liability and medical payments to others [S:nydfs-renters-insurance], which is the same set a condominium unit owners policy carries without the part that answers the structure [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]. The HO-4 form itself is not public, so this page describes the structure regulators describe rather than any insurer's wording.
protects: The tenant's own belongings, which the landlord's policy does not reach [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]
The tenant against personal liability for injuries others sustain at the home, including medical expenses and any resulting lawsuits, and damage to other people's property [S:nydfs-renters-insurance]
The cost of living elsewhere while the home cannot be used, through loss of use [S:nydfs-renters-insurance]
Medical payments to others, which responds without the argument about fault that liability cover involves [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]

commonlyCovers.item: Personal property, loss of use, personal liability and medical payments
commonlyCovers.note: These are the four parts a renters policy is described in [S:nydfs-renters-insurance], and they are the same four a condominium unit owners policy carries before it adds cover for the interior of the unit [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide].

Published regulator material lists fire, smoke, theft, vandalism, windstorm, hail, lightning, explosion, falling objects, weight of snow, ice and sleet, and water damage from plumbing or appliance failure [S:nydfs-renters-insurance].

commonlyCovers.item: Fire that follows an earthquake, in California
commonlyCovers.note: California law says that both homeowners and renters insurance must cover fire damage that is caused by or follows an earthquake [S:cdi-earthquake-insurance-guide]. The shaking is not covered; the fire afterwards is.

commonlyCovers.item: Liability at a minimum the regulator states
commonlyCovers.note: For renters policies, Coverage E Personal Liability is generally subject to a minimum of $100,000 and Coverage F Medical Payments to Others to a minimum of $1,000 [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide].

commonlyExcludes.note: That is the landlord's property and the landlord's policy. A rental dwelling policy states that tenant-owned personal property is not covered by it [S:statefarm-rental-dwelling], which is the same boundary seen from the other side.

Homeowners, renters and condominium policies do not cover damage from natural disasters such as earthquakes, floods and landslides [S:cdi-earthquake-insurance-guide]. Only the fire following an earthquake is required to be covered [S:cdi-earthquake-insurance-guide].
Insurance coverage for losses resulting from floods is generally not provided in a homeowners or renters policy [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide], and it is a separate policy on a separate form.

commonlyExcludes.item: The full value of certain categories of belongings
commonlyExcludes.note: Coverage on property especially susceptible to loss is limited, and those limited amounts are not separate limits in addition to the contents limit; they are included in it and represent the maximum paid for that type of property [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide].

limitsAndDeductibles: The contents limit is chosen rather than derived, because there is no dwelling limit to take a percentage of. That is the structural difference from a homeowners policy, where loss of use is normally limited to 20 percent of Coverage A [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide].

For renters policies the regulator states that personal liability is generally subject to a minimum of $100,000 and medical payments to others to a minimum of $1,000 [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide].

Special limits inside the contents limit cap categories such as jewelry and firearms, and they are a ceiling within the contents number rather than cover beside it [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide].
Contents flood, where taken, is a separate NFIP purchase and belongings can be insured up to $100,000 under a residential policy [S:nfip-agents-coverage].

Earthquake for a tenant is arranged separately. The California Earthquake Authority presents residential earthquake in four categories, one of which is renters [S:cea-home], and the FAIR Plan describes personal property coverage for the tenant of an apartment or single or multi-unit dwelling [S:cfp-dwelling-policy].

endorsements.note: Where a category exceeds its special limit, the route is scheduling or a floater rather than a larger contents limit, and California's marine article enumerates the floater types that may be written [S:ca-ccr-tit-10-2321].

endorsements.item: A separate earthquake policy for a tenant
endorsements.note: Available through the CEA as one of its four residential categories [S:cea-home]. It answers the shaking; the fire following is already required to be covered by the renters policy [S:cdi-earthquake-insurance-guide].
A tenant does not insure the building, so the flood purchase is the personal property side alone [S:nfip-agents-coverage].

relatedPolicies: Condominium unit owners insurance, which carries the same four parts and adds cover for the interior of the unit [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]
Landlord and rental dwelling insurance, which is the policy on the other side of the same boundary [S:statefarm-rental-dwelling]
Scheduled personal property, where a capped category needs to move onto its own form [S:ca-ccr-tit-10-2321]
underwritingInputs: What the belongings would cost to replace, since the contents limit is chosen rather than derived from a dwelling value [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]
Which capped categories are actually held, such as jewelry or firearms [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]
Whether an inventory exists listing items owned, dates purchased and price [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]
Whether the lease requires liability cover, and at what limit, against the stated minimums [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]
Whether earthquake or flood are real exposures at the address, since neither is in the policy [S:cdi-earthquake-insurance-guide][S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]

exposures.item: Assuming the landlord's policy reaches your belongings
exposures.note: It does not. The regulator states the landlord does not provide insurance for the tenant's personal property [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide], and a rental dwelling policy says the same from the landlord's side [S:statefarm-rental-dwelling]. This is the single most common misunderstanding on this line.

exposures.item: Liability that follows the tenant rather than the flat
exposures.note: Liability protection covers injuries others sustain at the tenant's home, including medical expenses and resulting lawsuits, and damage to other people's property [S:nydfs-renters-insurance]. A tenant with no policy meets that personally.

exposures.item: Nowhere to live after a fire
exposures.note: Loss of use is one of the four parts [S:nydfs-renters-insurance]. Without a policy the tenant pays for somewhere else while still liable under the lease, which is a cost the deposit does not touch.

exposures.item: Two perils the policy does not answer
exposures.note: Earthquake shake damage and flood are both outside it [S:cdi-earthquake-insurance-guide][S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide], and both are real in California. Only the fire following an earthquake is required to be covered [S:cdi-earthquake-insurance-guide].

exposures.item: A capped category treated as fully insured
exposures.note: The limited amounts for categories such as jewelry are inside the contents limit rather than additional to it [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide], so a large contents figure does not mean a large recovery on those items.

claimMitigation.item: Keep an inventory with dates and prices
claimMitigation.note: The regulator advises listing all items owned, the dates purchased and the price, and publishes a home inventory guide for it [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]. After a total loss the record is the practical obstacle rather than the limit.

claimMitigation.item: Set the contents limit from what replacement would cost
claimMitigation.note: There is no dwelling figure to derive it from, unlike a homeowners policy where loss of use runs at a percentage of Coverage A [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide], so the number has to be reasoned rather than inherited.

claimMitigation.item: Check the liability limit against the stated minimums
claimMitigation.note: The regulator gives $100,000 personal liability and $1,000 medical payments as the general minimums for renters policies [S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide], which is a floor rather than a recommendation.

claimMitigation.item: Treat earthquake and flood as separate decisions
claimMitigation.note: Neither is in the policy [S:cdi-earthquake-insurance-guide][S:cdi-residential-insurance-guide]. The CEA offers a renters category [S:cea-home] and contents flood is its own NFIP purchase [S:nfip-agents-coverage].

claimMitigation.item: Move a capped category onto its own form if it matters
claimMitigation.note: Scheduling or a floater is the route, and the floater types that may be written in California are enumerated by regulation [S:ca-ccr-tit-10-2321].

stateVariations.note: The requirement that both homeowners and renters insurance cover fire damage caused by or following an earthquake is California law as the regulator states it [S:cdi-earthquake-insurance-guide], and the CEA renters category and the FAIR Plan renters offering are Californian institutions [S:cea-home][S:cfp-dwelling-policy].

The description of the four coverage parts and the list of covered causes of loss cited on this page comes from New York regulator material [S:nydfs-renters-insurance]. It is used because it describes the ordinary structure of the line clearly, not because New York law governs a California tenancy. That source also records an exception to the landlord point: where the landlord knew of a prior hazardous condition, failed to correct it in a reasonable time and the tenant's property was damaged as a result [S:nydfs-renters-insurance].

author: Aaron Bollinger
